macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street rallies ahead of U.S. inflation report
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,104 points, or 2.2%, the S&P 500 gained 2.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 2.7% on Monday. Technology and semiconductor shares led the rebound, while investors awaited October CPI data.[2][7]

items.title: Fed’s Waller signals possible December rate hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he supports a 25-basis-point rate increase in December and that a 50-basis-point move could be considered if October core CPI is around 0.3% or higher. U.S. equity futures were little changed after the remarks.[1][5]

items.title: October CPI becomes key test for markets and Fed policy
items.summary: Economists expect October U.S. consumer prices to rise 0.3% month over month, with core prices increasing 0.2%. The report is expected to influence market expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening in December.[1][3]

items.title: Semiconductor stocks rebound sharply
items.summary: The Nasdaq-100 rose 3.4% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 6.85% in Monday trading. AMD climbed about 13.3% and Broadcom rose roughly 8.8%, while Nvidia fell about 4.2% amid company-specific concerns.[9]

items.title: Oil prices plunge amid improving geopolitical outlook
items.summary: Brent crude fell nearly 8% during the session as reports pointed to progress in U.S.-Iran discussions, easing concerns about energy supply disruptions and supporting a broader equity-market rally.[8]

items.title: European stocks advance; Infineon rallies on AI demand
items.summary: The STOXX 600 rose 0.7%, with European markets broadly higher as energy prices declined. Infineon gained 5.8% after reporting solid results and an upbeat fiscal-year outlook tied partly to AI-related demand.[6]

items.title: Companies scheduled to report earnings
items.summary: CoreWeave, TransDigm Group, Rigetti Computing, and D-Wave Quantum were among the notable companies scheduled to release quarterly results on Tuesday.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin Holds Near $75,000 as Crypto Market Declines
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 1% over the past 24 hours and traded near $75,000 amid broader risk-off pressure. Ether declined nearly 5%, while XRP also suffered losses and altcoins generally underperformed.

items.title: NYSE Selects Avalanche for Tokenized Securities Settlement
items.summary: The NYSE-affiliated digital trading platform selected Avalanche as the underlying ledger for clearing and settling tokenized securities. The proposed system would support continuous trading, subject to regulatory approval, and AVAX rose roughly 5.7%.

items.title: Canada Proposes Restrictions on Bank-Issued Crypto and Stablecoins
items.summary: Canada’s proposed budget legislation would bar federally regulated financial institutions from directly issuing cryptocurrencies and require stablecoins to be issued through regulated, independent non-financial subsidiaries. The framework would require redemption at face value and segregated reserves.

items.title: Kenya Faces IMF Pressure to Implement Crypto Travel Rule
items.summary: The IMF urged Kenya to require crypto companies to collect and share sender and recipient identity information under the Financial Action Task Force’s Travel Rule. The measure is intended to strengthen anti-money-laundering controls.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation Sells Another 1,000 ETH
items.summary: On-chain monitoring indicated that the Ethereum Foundation sold 1,000 ETH worth approximately $2.13 million. The transaction followed a previous sale and came as ETH traded near $2,131.

items.title: Alaska Plans to Tokenize Data Center and Energy Investments
items.summary: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy announced a partnership with Plural to tokenize investment contracts for data center and energy projects. The initiative is intended to give residents direct access to certain infrastructure investments through blockchain-based instruments.

items.title: SOL Drops Below $85
items.summary: Solana fell below $85, trading around $84.69 after declining 1.55% over 24 hours.

items.title: Pi Network Gains 10%
items.summary: Pi Network rose approximately 10% over 24 hours to about $0.0707, making it one of the session’s strongest-performing crypto assets.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic unveiled two new AI models aimed at advanced software engineering, scientific work, robotics, and autonomous agents. The company says the models are faster and improve on reasoning, coding, and visual analysis, while Mythos includes stronger safeguards and restricted access.[1]

items.title: LG Research releases K-EXAONE 2.5 with free API access
items.summary: LG AI Research released K-EXAONE 2.5, an updated model available through a free API after registration. LG reports more than 70% improvement across 24 benchmarks and positions it as competitive with leading agentic models.[2]

items.title: NVIDIA introduces GR00T 2 robotics model and simulation tools
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly introduced GR00T 2, an open-world action model, alongside robotics simulation tools, benchmarks, and agent workflows. Reported results reached 71% average success across 50 tasks with one demonstration and 95% with five.[3]

items.title: OpenAI rolls out Remix for ChatGPT Business and Enterprise
items.summary: OpenAI began rolling out Remix, which lets users copy an existing ChatGPT Site, generate a customized version, and continue editing it through conversation.[2]

items.title: GitHub Copilot becomes generally available in Slack and Microsoft Teams
items.summary: GitHub made Copilot integrations generally available in Slack and Microsoft Teams, enabling users to investigate bugs, create issues, draft fixes, open pull requests, and review code changes through workplace chats.[2]

items.title: NXP launches edge platform for physical AI and robotics
items.summary: NXP Semiconductors launched a unified robotics platform designed to deploy secure physical-AI systems on edge devices, reflecting continued investment in AI-enabled robotics outside the cloud.[2]

items.title: Illinois governor calls for federal AI safety and data-center rules
items.summary: Illinois Gov. J.B. Pritzker proposed federal requirements for AI risk assessment, testing, and monitoring, alongside privacy protections and energy- and water-efficiency standards for data centers.[4]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Take-Two plans revivals of legacy franchises
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said the company is working on reviving several dormant or underused franchises, though no specific titles were named.[1]

items.title: GTA 6 preloads reportedly begin ahead of launch
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly began preloading ahead of its November 19 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S; the PC version is expected later.[4]

items.title: Take-Two reports weaker quarterly bookings amid GTA 6 anticipation
items.summary: Take-Two missed quarterly net-bookings expectations while highlighting strong Grand Theft Auto V performance and rising anticipation for GTA VI.[2]

items.title: Paramount’s games division reportedly cuts jobs
items.summary: Paramount’s merged game division is reportedly reducing staff and scaling down some projects following the company’s Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition.[6]

items.title: Bit Reactor employees reportedly laid off
items.summary: Several employees at Bit Reactor, the studio behind Star Wars: Zero Company, were reportedly laid off after an extended furlough affecting much of the staff.[7]

items.title: Football Manager adds wheelchair representation
items.summary: The latest Football Manager reportedly allows players to create a manager who uses a wheelchair, as part of Sports Interactive’s broader accessibility and inclusion efforts.[8]
